summary: Scourge boss that can spawn in the Nightmare realm depending on the monsters present; the wiki gives stats and no individual lore.

name: Gianna
summary: Deception rogue (the Master of Disguise). Backstory: she worked at the Theopolis Thespian Society in Oriath, and her early contracts involve Templar uniforms. Unlocked by a Vinderi contract.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: Theopolis Thespian Society; "To unlock Gianna, run a contract with Vinderi"

name: Gravicius Reborn
summary: Former Act 3 general, resurrected Syndicate member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Greust
summary: Azmeri-friendly villager of the Forest Encampment (his shrine and necklace follow Azmeri custom) who becomes the avatar of Ralakesh through a washed-up Vaal relic in Act 7; the exile must kill him to force Ralakesh back into the relic. Helena asks that his necklace be laid at the Azmeri shrine in the Northern Forest.

alt_summaries.summary: Forest Encampment weapon/armour vendor and hunter, hostile to Oriathans; gives Intruders in Black. (Helena calls the village Azmeri; Greust's own ethnicity is not stated in the sources read.)

name: Grigor
summary: Poet-scholar of the Sarn Encampment who knows the ode 'Of Jewels and Eternity', sends the Exile to the Gemling Queen, then after Piety and Dominus; Maramoa says to 'look upon Grigor to see what life entails under Piety's influence'.

name: Guardian of the Void: Chimera
summary: One of the Shaper's four Guardians of the Void; defeating it yields the Fragment of the Chimera, part of the Key to the Crucible.

sources.locator: The Shaper section: 'Fragment of the Chimera'

name: Guardian of the Void: Hydra
summary: One of the Shaper's four Guardians of the Void; defeating it yields the Fragment of the Hydra, part of the Key to the Crucible.

sources.locator: The Shaper section: 'Fragment of the Hydra'

name: Guardian of the Void: Minotaur
summary: One of the Shaper's four Guardians of the Void; defeating it yields the Fragment of the Minotaur, part of the Key to the Crucible.

sources.locator: The Shaper section: 'Fragment of the Minotaur'

name: Guardian of the Void: Phoenix
summary: One of the Shaper's four Guardians of the Void; defeating it yields the Fragment of the Phoenix, part of the Key to the Crucible.

sources.locator: The Shaper section: 'Fragment of the Phoenix'

name: Guatelitzi
summary: Figure known only from the flavour text of Guatelitzi's Ablation (drop location Atziri's Temple): as a young man he was found among prisoners 'preparing their living bodies for sacrifice', and the High Priests recognised his inclinations and gave him a higher calling. Vaal placement is inferred from the Atziri's Temple drop location, not stated.

chronology.relative: Vaal era (inferred from Atziri's Temple drop location; no date stated)

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'Young Guatelitzi was found moving among the prisoners, preparing their living bodies for sacrifice. The High Priests recognised his inclinations, and gave him a higher calling.'

name: Guff "Tiny" Grenn
summary: Syndicate member from the Brinerot warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Gwennen, the Gambler
summary: Kalguuran gambler and former rebel who avoids Kingsmarch because Johan, scarred by her, could recognise her and expose surviving rebels.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran gambler and Expedition NPC who sells unidentified equipment and takes Broken Circle artifacts.
Kalguuran missing in the islands; rescued in The Grand Expedition; wife of Rog per 0.5.

name: Hailrake
summary: Boss of the Tidal Island holding Doctor Opden's Medicine Chest.

name: Haku, Armourmaster
summary: Karui forsaken master (armour); Syndicate member. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Hargan
summary: Sarn Encampment weapon/armour vendor; fence who seeks Victario's busts for his 'return to Oriath' fund.

alt_summaries.summary: Sarn Encampment trader who points out Doedre and sends the exile after the Wings of Vastiri.

name: Hayoxi
summary: Figure called 'The Architect of Destruction' in the flavour text of Hayoxi's Fulmination, who laid explosive powder under the royal temple 'one pinch at a time' and never found the courage to light it. Identity beyond the flavour text is not recorded in the corpus. Placement in the Vaal era is inferred from the royal-temple setting.

chronology.relative: Vaal era (inferred from royal-temple setting; no date stated)

sources.locator: flavour_text: 'The Architect of Destruction slipped explosive powder under the royal temple one pinch at a time. For years, he clung to that, never finding the courage to light it.'

name: Hector Titucius, Eternal Servant
summary: One of the Undying: murderer of the Maraketh Sekhema Asenath (the Golden Sekhema), who again guards her Wings of Vastiri in the Bath House; Hargan wants the Wings to ransom back to the Maraketh.

alt_summaries.summary: Ezomyte-born gemling general, 'Scourge of the Maraketh', destroyed by Deshret's storm trap in 1333 IC.

name: Helena
summary: Young Oriathan Ebony Legion woman rescued from the Chamber of Sins; joins the Forest Encampment and directs the Lorrata plan.

alt_summaries.summary: Former Piety expedition member at the Bridge Encampment; tells of Maligaro's secret passage and Greust's memorial.

name: Herius
summary: Priest 'of the Order' listed as a Twilight Order member under Torvian, Hand of the Saviour. No further detail in sources read.

name: Hilda
summary: Monster hunter and Atlas Master (Hilda's Campsite); her endgame quest Hilda's Hunting has the Exile track and defeat four Great Beasts.

sources.locator: Atlas Masters: Hilda, a monster hunter
Quest Complete: 'You have tracked and defeated four Great Beasts.'

name: Hillock, the Blacksmith
summary: Act 1 boss Hillock resurrected by the Mastermind and joined the Syndicate. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

alt_summaries.summary: First boss of Act 1 (Twilight Strand); exiled criminal turned zombie; later resurrected as Hillock, the Blacksmith of the Syndicate.
First boss: an undead exile (Hillock of Slaugh) with a sword in his chest guarding the end of the Twilight Strand; killed in Enemy at the Gate.

name: Huck
summary: Former soldier who joined the Ring after his discharge and hunts a lost friend, Enoch, who died in Templar research on augmentations. Hireable in Heists; unlocked by a Karst contract, and his contract unlocks Niles.

sources.locator: Lead; Personal Questline; "To unlock Huck, run a contract with Karst" (Niles page); "Took it out not long after joining the Ring"

name: Queen Hyrri Ngamaku
summary: Kaom's niece, archer, led Karui archers at Lioneye's Watch and the Karui at the Grain Gate; after Kaom's death guided the remaining 500 Karui families home, became queen, had a child with Victario (per wiki) and was succeeded by her daughter Ahuana; later vanished.

sources.locator: Lore: 'She later became the queen and had a child with Victario ... succeeded by her daughter, Ahuana'

alt_summaries.summary: Niece of King Kaom; trained in archery at Thebrus and led Karui women archers in the ambush that defeated Marceus Lioneye at Lioneye's Watch (Purity Rebellion). After Kaom's corruption she led 500 Karui families home to Ngamakanui, became queen, had a child with Victario, then vanished leading an army against an unknown threat; succeeded by Ahuana. General of the Karui legion in Legion league (3.7.0).
Kaom's niece; led the bow-women whose arrows surprised Lioneye and succeeded Kaom as Karui queen after he left.

name: Icius Perandus
summary: Eternal Empire-era scholar and translator of Vaalish texts (name suggests the Perandus family, not verified); hid four Golden Pages in the Sarn Archives; friend of Siosa; also cited as author of the 'Chronicle of Atzoatl'.

alt_summaries.summary: Scholar to the Empire, translated Vaal artefacts for Malachai, hid the Golden Pages, joined the Order of the Djinn.

name: Ignagduk, the Bog Witch
summary: Azak tribe unique boss of The Azak Bog in Act 3, who holds stolen children; slain in the Tribal Vengeance quest, dropping Ignagduk's Ghastly Spear.

sources.locator: Infobox (boss Ignagduk, the Bog Witch); lead: 'Find Ignagduk in the Azak village'

name: Ikiaho
summary: Chieftain of the Arohongui tribe, loyal to Arohongui; vouched for Rakiata in the Halls of the Dead and tells that Ramako was impersonated.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: Iktab, the Deathlord
summary: Undead lord assisting Ekbab in the Bone Pits.

sources.locator: Walkthrough 'Defeat Ekbab, Ancient Steed and Iktab'

name: Incarnation of Dread
summary: Warped memory-boss of the Originator's threads. Moment of Reverence: Valdo's promise of a brighter future.

name: Incarnation of Fear
summary: Warped memory-boss of the Originator's threads. Moment of Trauma: Valdo's fury at Zana.

name: Incarnation of Neglect
summary: Warped memory-boss of the Originator's threads. Moment of Loneliness: Zana asks Valdo to admire the Atlas; 'Not now, Zana!'. Interpretive: its Valdo/Zana 'Not now, Zana!' memory suggests it embodies Valdo's neglect; the wiki does not state this.

name: The Infinite Hunger
summary: Primary champion of the Tangle fought in the Seething Chyme.

name: Inya, the Unbearable Whispers
summary: Boss of the Pale Council encounter in The Pale Court (Prophecy system). Introduced in 2.3.0 and removed in 3.17.0 per the wiki; in 3.0.0 the Pale Council was rebalanced and Inya became a drop source for Inya's Epiphany.

sources.locator: Infobox: location = The Pale Court; Drops: 'guaranteed to drop Inya's Epiphany ... if she was the last one to be killed ... the sequence ... is random'; Version history 3.17.0 'Removed from the game'

name: Irasha
summary: Maraketh akhara of Highgate and rival of Tasuni for rule after Oyun's disappearance. Her twin sister died of a scorpion's sting during the womanhood trial; she asks the exile to kill Shakari and may receive the Sekhema Feather.

name: Isla, the Engineer
summary: Engineer building Kingsmarch's map devices and the Recombinator; her letter ('I'm so happy you're alive!') hints at a past connection with the Exile and mentions Kalguuran runes' strange effect on portals.

sources.locator: Lead and Lore: "a skillset she acquired working under Inquisitor Dominus"

alt_summaries.summary: Engineer rogue hireable for Heists; per the wiki she worked under Inquisitor Dominus ~20 years before the PoE1 campaign and designed The Unbreakable, the design of which was stolen by the Templar. Also operates the Recombinator and Kalguuran Map Devices in Kingsmarch.
Former Templar chosen by Venarius to maintain the Map Device; now in Kingsmarch corresponding with Zana and experimenting with Kalguuran runes in map devices.

name: It That Fled
summary: Breach-realm creature that fled the Breachlords' rule and is listed among Immortal Syndicate members; most Syndicate members fear it. (Not in Keepers league.) Identity beyond that unclear.

sources.locator: 13:26 "being from the breach realm who fled the rule of the Breachlords"; 17:53 most members terrified of it
restrictions: It That Fled cannot appear in the Immortal Syndicate

name: It That Was Esh
summary: Hive Colony boss fought together with It That Was Tul (PoE1 3.27/3.28, PoE2 0.5.0). Per Ailith it is not the original Esh but possibly Esh's leftover remains after the fusion into Xesht.

alt_summaries.summary: Former Breachlord boss in the Hive Colony (paired with Tul).

name: It That Was Tul
summary: Hive Colony boss fought together with It That Was Esh (PoE1 3.27/3.28, PoE2 0.5.0); drops the Breachlord Sac / Breach rings. Per Ailith it is not the original Tul but possibly Tul's leftover remains after the fusion into Xesht.

alt_summaries.summary: Former Breachlord boss in the Hive Colony.

name: Ixan Keita
summary: Founder of House Keita, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

name: Ixchel
summary: Vaal Order of the Djinn member ('Godstealer') who stole the sleeping body of Yaomac for the Order; captured while infiltrating the Temple of Chaos and became the Trialmaster.

name: Emperor Izaro
summary: The last Phrecian emperor, impotent from inbreeding, who built the Lord's Labyrinth in 1317 IC to choose a successor. Sealed inside by Chitus. The Exile can still meet him as an enemy in the Labyrinth.

sources.locator: section 'Reign of Izaro'; section 'Reign of Chitus'

alt_summaries.summary: Last Phrecian Emperor; childless, he built the Lord's Labyrinth to choose a successor. Chitus won it, then sealed Izaro inside. The exile fights him in the Labyrinth.

name: Jado
summary: Member of the Order of the Djinn first met in Interlude 2; reveals Jun has been rebuilding the Order in secret for 20 years since Catarina's fall. Atlas Master in 0.5, unlocked via an anomaly map near the Atlas start.

sources.locator: first mentioned by Jado, NPC introduced in Interlude 2
Atlas Masters: Jado of the Order of the Djinn
Jado questline unlocked by completing an anomaly map near the starting location

alt_summaries.summary: Order of the Djinn agent who infiltrated the Sel Khari to guard the First Barya; promises the Order will 'be there' in Oriath.

name: Jaetai, Vaal Advisor
summary: Vaal advisor to Atziri mentioned only on the flavour text of Atziri's Foible.

name: Jamanra, the Risen King
summary: Faridun leader resurrected by the Countess, who locks the Halani Gates, summons sandstorms, and is later executed by Sekhema Asala as Jamanra the Abomination.

sources.locator: Quest 'Defeat Jamanra, the Risen King' / 'Defeat Jamanra, the Abomination'

alt_summaries.summary: Faridun revolutionary leader resurrected by corruption in PoE2 Act 2, given death by Asala.

name: Janus Perandus
summary: Great-grandson of Chitus Perandus; former Order of the Djinn member and gambling addict who betrayed the order to Catarina and joined the Syndicate.

alt_summaries.summary: Chitus' great-grandson; Immortal Syndicate member who betrayed the Order of the Djinn.

name: Johan, the King's Hand
summary: Kalguuran official sent to execute Kingsmarch's Charter as the King's Hand and Treasurer; admits loyalty to both the King and the Charter's law; tolerates 'less than upstanding' residents so long as he sees no sedition. He bears a scar given by Gwennen.

name: Julius Perandus
summary: Father of Chitus.

name: Jun Ortoi
summary: Master NPC, survivor and guardian of the Forbidden Vaults of the Order of the Djinn; hunts the Syndicate after its killing of her order. Introduced in Betrayal; Act 9 quest "The Immortal Syndicate".

sources.locator: 1:05 Jun Ortoi, Order of the Djinn

alt_summaries.summary: Veteran Order of the Djinn member; in PoE2 mentioned as rebuilding the Order since Catarina's fall 20 years earlier.

name: Justicar Casticus
summary: Templar justicar in the Control Blocks whose Eyes of Zeal give entry to the Templar Courts.

name: Kadavrus the Defiler
summary: Necromancer boss of the Fetid Pool who was raising the dead rhoa.

name: Kahuturoa
summary: Chieftain of the Rongokurai tribe per the Karui page (some history text files him with the Ramako tribe); recounts Ramako, Kitava's defeat and the Maraketh 'thousand years'.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: Kaimana
summary: Karui healer-alchemist at Ngakanu working on a Blood Fever cure; sends the Exile for the Great White shark's fin. Says 'If the ancestors see you... you can never truly die'.

name: K'aj A'alai
summary: Third demon of the Vaal Temple map boss trio, variants of the Atziri trio; all released with Sacrifice of the Vaal.

name: K'aj Q'ura
summary: Unique demon boss in the Vaal Temple map, a variant of the Atziri trio; uses Demon Cleave (Corrupted Blood) and Cyclone.

name: K'aj Y'ara'az
summary: Unique demon boss in the Vaal Temple map; one of a trio that are variants of the Atziri trio of the Apex of Sacrifice. Uses Dual Strike and Fire Enrage.

name: Kalandra
summary: Ancient being with an owl's body and human head, trapped in the Lake of Kalandra since the primordial era; she observes the world, scorns gods as 'thieves of virtue', and plans escape. Visited by the Order of the Djinn and the Clayshaper among others. Namesake of the Mirror of Kalandra.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient owl-bodied being trapped in her lake since the primordial era; disdains gods ('thieves of virtue') and is said to have counselled Sin on creating the Beast.

name: Kanu
summary: First Mate of the Aurora May, listed among Twilight Order members: he is courted by Benedictus ('Accept Utopia!'), betrays Makoru, then reveals the Beast is kept in Oriath and is attacked by Tavakai ('Let the ancestors judge him') - death is implied.

sources.locator: Confront Kanu and the First Herald; Defeat Benedictus

name: King Kaom
summary: Karui king who took Lioneye's Watch, was lured to Highgate by Malachai's voice posing as Tukohama and slain; defeated in Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: King of the Karui (chieftain of the Ngamahu tribe) who invaded Lioneye's Watch for Voll's Purity Rebellion; later deceived by a vision from the 'black spirit', entered the Highgate mines, was corrupted by Malachai and sealed in with the Beast by Deshret; boss in Kaom's Stronghold (Act 4) holding the Eye of Fury.

name: Karst
summary: Lockpicking rogue in the Rogue Harbour; a Ring member (Kurai: 'assist member Karst') who aids the exile on the Trial Run contract and whose hire unlocks Huck.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: "Talk to Karst, the Lockpick, the rogue that aids you"
'The Ring' dialogue: 'assist member Karst on this job'

name: Kastov
summary: Governor of Stridevolf in the Eternal Empire who joined High Templar Voll's Purity Rebellion in 1333 IC against the gemling thaumatocracy. Per the Victario page, unlike Voll, Ondar, Geofri and Adus he did not turn undead or into a ghost in the in-game present.

sources.locator: intro paragraph: 'Governor Kastov of Stridevolf' listed among Voll's allies with Lord Mayor Ondar, Victario, Archbishop Geofri and Commander Adus

paragraph 'In 1333 IC, Victario supported the Purity Rebellion ... along with Kastov, Lord Mayor Ondar, Archbishop Geofri and Commander Adus'; and 'neither Victario nor Kastov turned into the undead or a ghost'
section '==Members==' > Purity Rebellion rebels: '** [[Kastov]], Governor of [[Stridevolf]]'

name: Kelari
summary: The assassin Djinn bound to serve the Sekhema Varashta as penance; an invulnerable minion of the Disciple of Varashta ascendancy that stays inert in its barya until commanded.

sources.locator: section 'Overview': 'The three Djinns are Ruzhan the fire Djinn, Navira the water Djinn, and Kelari the assassin Djinn.'
section 'Overview': 'Each the Djinn are invulnerable minions that remain inert in their Baryas until the Disciple commands them to unleash their powers.'

name: Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun
summary: Vaal High Priest of the Sun whose writings Alva cites about research in the Temple of Kopec (device/time gateway); boss in the Temple of Kopec defeated by the Exile in PoE2 Act 3.

sources.locator: Quest 'Defeat Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun'

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal high priest of the Sun God in the Temple of Kopec whose research leads to the time gateway.

name: Kiloava
summary: Chieftain of the Valako tribe, absorbed by Kaom's conquests; speaks on how tribes may change their gods.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: King Cadigan
summary: Mysterious tyrant-king of Kalguur whose name all kings share (possibly one person extending life by artifice); spies on subjects, instituted shipment taxes, has his eye on Wraeclast, and in PoE2 ordered Vaal artifacts brought home.

sources.locator: Negative outcomes: 'The King decided to institute a one-time tax'

alt_summaries.summary: Current infamous ruler of Kalguur, always named Cadigan; rumoured to use artifice to extend life and spy on subjects; Kalguuran NPCs avoid speaking of him. In PoE2 he orders Vaal artifacts brought to Kalguur.

name: King Cadigan the Third
summary: Kalguuran king who, after reading the Vaal Cataclysm as an 'Omen', commissioned the first expedition to Wraeclast with the Triskelion Flame and banned gems after the Azmeri panicked at the sight of one.

chronology.relative: Shortly after the Vaal Cataclysm (first Kalguuran expedition)

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran king who commissioned the expedition and banned gems after Azmeri panic over gem drawings.
Ordered the first Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast carrying the Triskelion Flame; banned collection of virtue gems after the Azmeri's fearful reaction.

name: Kira, Servant of Garukhan
summary: Maraketh warrior who leads a dekhara (warband), obsessed with Garukhan, the 'Vulture of the Wastes'. She kidnaps Sekhema Oyun to sacrifice her, hoping to become a 'Red Sekhema' and wearing the Sekhema Feather; the exile kills her and Garukhan but fails to save Oyun.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4 weapon and armour vendor in Highgate.

name: Commander Kirac
summary: Tracker and officer of Oriath's volunteer Citizen Vanguard, later Commander; younger brother of Baran. In legacy epilogue quests he asked the Exile to find Baran, who had fallen in with 'radical' Zana Caeserius. Sits in the Karui Shores War Room, issues maps, pinnacle invitations and Atlas Books of Skill, calls the Exile 'Godslayer' and backs the Maven as 'the best of our terrible options'. Took Sirus's blow meant for Zana. His dialogue says the Maven resurrects Baran for her games.

sources.locator: Karui Shores: Helena directs the player to Commander Kirac in the War Room, who gives a Tier 1 map
quote: 'My younger brother, Baran, fell in with a radical by the name of Zana Caeserius'
KiracOnBaranResurrectionTwo; Introduction: 'tracker and officer in Oriath's new Citizen Vanguard'
Kirac: 'She's the best of our terrible options'

alt_summaries.summary: Oriath officer. In the older Epilogue (v3.9-3.16, 'Picking Up the Pieces', now removed) Officer Kirac sends the exile to the Templar Laboratory to find his brother Baran and learn about Zana; in the current Epilogue Commander Kirac waits in the War Room at Karui Shores and hands the exile the first Map (A Call to Arms).

name: Kishara
summary: Vaal explorer from Atziri's time who fell out of favour; Atziri seized her ship and sacrificed its crew. She hid Kishara's Star near the Causeway and her descendants formed the Brinerot clan.

name: Kole
summary: Unique demon monster in The Lunaris Temple Level 1 (Act 3), with a high-damage Ground Smash and a chain pull. Per the wiki's lore section (attributed to Grigor), Kole was an Oriathan rapist whom Piety used in her experiments. A stronger Carnage variant appeared in the Tower Map (2.4.0-3.1.0).

chronology.relative: Act 3 (c. Piety's experiments; relative date unknown)

sources.locator: Infobox: location = The Lunaris Temple Level 1 (Act 3); Lore: 'According to Grigor, Kole was an Oriathan ... before Piety used him in her experiments'

name: Korell Goya
summary: Syndicate member from the Redblade warband. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Kraityn
summary: Bandit lord of the Broken Bridge, exiled from Theopolis in 1598 IC for avarice, larceny, murder and more (Letters of Exile).

name: Krutog, Lord of Kin
summary: Kin Tyrant boss of the Volcanic Warrens on the Isle of Kin, killed in Land of the Kin.

name: K'Tash, the Hate Shepherd
summary: Scourge boss (K'tash, the Hate Shepherd) that can spawn in the Nightmare realm depending on the monsters present; the wiki gives stats but no individual lore.

name: Kurai
summary: Administrator of the Rogue Harbour; starts the introductory Rogue Harbour quest in Act 6 and hands out the first contract.

name: Kurgal, the Blackblooded
summary: Abyssal Lich, commander of the Lightless and servant of Kulemak. Boss in the Lich's Tomb in Delve (depth 90+); born from a stone golem Kulemak created in his bargain with Aul.

alt_summaries.summary: Kurgal is an Abyssal Lich and one of Kulemak's three most powerful servants commanding the Lightless.
Lich Lord under Kulemak; a Delve boss in PoE1 (The Lich's Tomb, depth 90+) and named as a PoE2 Lich Lord by the Lurking Creature.

name: Kylian Cyaxan
summary: Founder of House Cyaxan, one of the four Great Founders who rebelled against Emperor Tyndarus Phrecius.

name: Lachlann of Endless Lament
summary: Lachlann the Lost, a Count of the Cemetery of the Eternals seeking to reunite with his family; the Exile puts him to rest after the Memorial Gate opens.

name: Lani
summary: Leader of the rebel encampment at Overseer's Tower (Act 5) and hub NPC of the Oriath Docks in Act 10; she tells how Vilenta betrayed her and Bannon, is fond of Bannon, and rewards the exile after Kitava's fall.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui slave rebel at Overseer's Tower who rewards the Exile; knows of Kitava's Torments; says she 'helped bring this curse down upon Oriath'.

name: Lavianga
summary: Karui scholar-advisor to Kaom.

name: Lazhwar
summary: Archbishop of the Eternal Faith whose thaumaturgy and Eternal Laboratory work preceded Malachai's.

name: Leitis
summary: Ogham prisoner held by the Executioner; freed by the Exile, and sends the Exile after Count Geonor.

name: Leo, Master of the Arena
summary: Pit master of the Sarn arena; forsaken master of PvP missions. Immortal Syndicate member in Betrayal league (3.5.0).

name: Lilly Roth
summary: Pirate captain and granddaughter of Weylam Roth; her ship brings the exile to Lioneye's Watch (Act 6) and back to Oriath (Act 10). She is the gem vendor, asks the exile to clear the Twilight Strand, to retrieve The Teardrop (map to Tsoatha) and, after Kitava's death, offers to sail the exile away.

sources.locator: Lilly offers to ferry exile to Oriath
Lilly: drowned Oriathans washing ashore after cultists plunder refugee ships
Lilly: Templar privateers took the Teardrop; she and her grandfather plan to sail to Tsoatha

alt_summaries.summary: Ship captain who ferries survivors from Oriath to Wraeclast.

name: Missionary Lorandis
summary: Twilight Order preacher in Kingsmarch who sends the Exile to Arastas to take an oath to the Saviour and later leads them to the Herald; cries 'We were trying to... save you' when the ambush turns.

sources.locator: Follow the Preacher; Survive the ambush
Follow the Preacher / Survive the ambush

alt_summaries.summary: Twilight Order preacher in Kingsmarch/Arastas who lures the Exile to take an oath to the Saviour and is dismayed when Torvian ambushes them.

name: Lorrata
summary: Giant tree over the Vaal Ruins in the Wetlands, said to be the oldest tree in the area and planted by ancient Azmeri travellers (per Eramir); its roots held the Vaal doors shut until poisoned by the Exile with Maligaro's Spike and the Baleful Gem.

name: Lucan Octavius
summary: Wealthy Oriathan alchemist, Tane's master; publicly genial but violent and lustful in private; killed by Tane, who was exiled for it.

name: Lumerius
summary: Son of the Countess; datamine lists him as an Act 5 boss in Oriath. Role unverified.

sources.locator: paragraph 2: 'She also has a son named Lumerius'

alt_summaries.summary: Son of the Countess whom she 'seeks to use to fulfill her agenda'. His role in the Order is not clarified in any source read.

name: Lundara
summary: Twin sister Sekhema; possibly Lunaris.

name: Lycia, Herald of the Scourge
summary: Former Templar scholar and keeper of forbidden knowledge who, disillusioned by the truth of Innocence's origins and the Templars' unmarked ossuary bones, made a pact with the Scourge demon Beidat for immortality; imprisoned in the Sanctum she is its fourth-floor boss and league antagonist.

chronology.relative: lived sometime after the Eternal Empire's founding; exact date unknown (video guesses c. 1000-1300 IC)

sources.locator: page summary: former Templar, necromancy and lithomancy, immortality in pact with Beidat

alt_summaries.summary: Former Templar who uncovered the real story of Sin and Innocence.

name: Maata
summary: Chieftain of the Tawhoa tribe; her text discusses the Vaal.

chronology.relative: deceased Karui chieftain, resides in the Halls of the Dead

name: Makoru
summary: Captain of the Aurora May under the Meridian Free Traders; ferries the Exile around Ngamakanui and gives the logbook.

sources.locator: Makoru: Captain of the Aurora May
Talk to Makoru; Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon

alt_summaries.summary: Captain of the Aurora May who ferries the Exile around the Karui islands under the Meridian Free Traders.
Captain of the Aurora May, Karui, daughter of Tavakai; betrayed by Kanu and taken by her father when he flees with the Weapon.

name: Malachai
summary: Laureate Thaumaturge to Chitus, creator of the gemling legions and Rapture Device. Spared by Voll, he entered the Beast and caused the Cataclysm. Defeated by the exile in Act 4.

sources.locator: intro paragraph 5 and section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'; 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Chitus's Laureate Thaumaturge. He persuaded Voll to spare him, built the Rapture Device, and used it at Highgate to breach the Belly of the Beast, triggering the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC).

Chitus's master thaumaturge, spared by Emperor Voll after promising 'the end to thaumaturgy'; built the Rapture Device, entered the Beast to take its power, and brought on the Cataclysm; final boss of Act 4 in the Black Core.
Act 4 boss whose lieutenants Shavronne, Maligaro and Doedre are revived and harvested in Part Two.
Thaumaturge following in Doryani's footsteps.

name: Maligaro
summary: Inquisitor Maligaro, flesh artist of the Godless Three; burned by Voll, his spirit lived on in Maligaro's Sanctum; killed in Act 7.

alt_summaries.summary: Thaumaturge of Malachai's Godless Three; worked in the Chamber of Sins; burned by Voll; returns in Act 4 as the Inquisitor boss.
Thaumaturgist and Malachai disciple who worked flesh in the Chamber of Sins; his spirit is killed in Act 7.

name: Maramoa
summary: Karui exile from Ngamakanui (sentenced 1597 IC) who survives in the Sarn Encampment; he appears in Acts 3 and 8. In Act 8 he warns of the Gemling Legion and of the awakened Solaris and Lunaris, and sends the exile to take the Sun and Moon Orbs from their devotees.

alt_summaries.summary: Exile at the Sarn Encampment who gives Lost in Love and Sever the Right Hand; uses Karui terms (makoru, waikoama) so is probably Karui (inferred). The 'leader' role in the earlier draft was not supported.

name: General Marceus Lioneye
summary: Eternal Empire general and leader of the Gemling Legion; archer with a virtue gem in one eye; defeated by Hyrri's ambush at Lioneye's Watch during the Purity Rebellion. (General of the Eternal Empire legion in Legion league, 3.7.0.)

sources.locator: Purity Rebellion: Kaom wore his head on his belt

alt_summaries.summary: Gem-eyed archer general at Lioneye's Watch, killed by Kaom.
Eternal Empire general and leader of the Gemling Legion, a one-eyed (virtue gem) archer; sent to drive off Kaom during the Purity Rebellion and killed at Lioneye's Watch, which is named for him.

name: Marylene
summary: Victario's lover, died shielding him at the Grain Gate.

name: Matiki
summary: Karui held on one of the Act 4 islands (rotating location) whose rescue unlocks the Eye of Hinekora and Trial of the Ancestors.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui figure freed in PoE2 Act 4 who leads the Exile to the Eye of Hinekora and the Trial of the Ancestors.

name: The Maven
summary: Primordial claimant of the Atlas who is 'bored with the realm she has given', serving only her own amusement; not the Elder but to be feared. She witnesses map bosses and traps challengers in her Memory Game. Her origin is unresolved.

sources.locator: Envoy: 'She is not The Elder, but you are right to fear her.'

name: Maxarius
summary: Per the Sanctum relic texts (as recounted in the wiki and video), Maxarius, the first High Templar, was in truth Innocence himself - a charlatan who stole the Descry symbol from fire-terrified newcomers, used their fear, and vilified his brother Sin to ascend.

chronology.relative: ancient, when the Azmeri still lived in the Azmerian mountains

sources.locator: [28:00]-[30:30] relics reveal Maxarius = Innocence; quote 'a charlatan, a liar and a power seeker'
===Templar history (line ~188): "The very first High Templar, Maxarius, was not Innocence's chosen, as was told, but Innocence himself."
Lore: "He posed himself as Maxarius, the first High Templar, and vilified his own brother as the Original Evil."

name: Medici Perandus
summary: Member of the Perandus family styled 'Prefect to the Treasury'. The corpus knows him only from the flavour text of the Perandus Signet; no dated action is recorded, so his era is unknown.

sources.locator: section '===Medici Perandus===': 'Medici Perandus, "Prefect to the Treasury", is a member of the Perandus family only referred to by the flavour text of Perandus Signet.'
section '==Members==' > Perandus family: 'Medici Perandus, Prefect to the Treasury'

name: Medved
summary: Leader of the Druids of the Broken Circle who claimed to peer into the past. He pioneered culling a horror species, challenged the horrors' leader alone and vanished. He returns as a horror boss in PoE1 (Medved, Feller of Heroes).

chronology.relative: Expedition era, thousands of years before PoE1

sources.locator: section 'The Kalguur' (Broken Circle, Priesthood, Medved's challenge)

alt_summaries.summary: Druid of the Broken Circle who discovered soul vapour leaving corpses toward gems; became a horror champion, Medved, Feller of Heroes.
Leader of the Druids of the Broken Circle of Kalguur, rumoured to see the future by peering into the past; experiments with virtue gems.
Ancient Kalguuran whose tomb opens the Expedition storyline; not as dead as expected.

name: Meginord
summary: Figure referred to only in flavour text and names of unique belts (e.g. Meginord's Girdle, Meginord's Vise). The wiki says he ruled a northern part of Wraeclast, but it is unclear whether he is a person or a naming pun.

sources.locator: Intro: 'a figure only mentioned in the flavour text and names of unique items'; Lore: 'it is unclear whether the character was intended to be called north-north'

name: Mektul, the Forgemaster
summary: Boss of The Molten Vault in Act 3, defeated in the Treasures of Utzaal quest; drops The Hammer of Kamasa.

name: Ascension Trials
summary: PoE2's three-trial system (Sekhemas, Chaos, and a planned third) that gates ascendancy. Each trial is tied to a Wraeclastian culture. Four tiers of trials give 2 ascendancy points each for 8 total.

name: The Atlas of Worlds (concept)
summary: The endgame structure of PoE1: a web of alternate worlds ('maps') reached through the Map Device. Wiki lore says it was either found or created by the Elder as a hunting ground; after the Elder's defeat other powers (Maven, Eldritch Horrors, the Originator) contest it. PoE2 has its own, separate Atlas whose Precursor Towers are mentioned in PoE1 wiki lore.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' / 'The Elder and the Shaper'
lead: 'The Atlas of Worlds may have originally been created as a feeding ground for the Elder'

name: Atlas Passive Skill Tree
summary: The upgrade tree of the PoE1 Atlas endgame, spent with Atlas passive skill points and Atlas passive respec points. Points come from Atlas Book of Skill items and from quest rewards (for example The Elder, The Maven's Game, The Searing Exarch, The Eater of Worlds). The wiki counts 9 Atlas Books of Skill for 12 Atlas passive points in total.

sources.locator: 'List of Book of Skills' intro: 'There are 9 Atlas Book of Skills in Wraeclast, for a total of 12 Atlas passive points'; the earned points are shown by hovering over the counter 'at the bottom of the Atlas passive tree'
Walkthrough 'Use the Atlas Book of Skill' and Quest Complete log: 'gained 1 Atlas Passive Skill Point and 2 Atlas Passive Respec Points'

name: Azmeri Spirits and Wisps
summary: Azmeri spirits appear as wisps leading hunters to monsters, introduced with Dawn of the Hunt; Delwyn at Hunting Grounds teaches the hunt; the Spirit Walker ascendancy (0.5) controls Stag, Owl, Bear spirits.

sources.locator: Spirit Walker (Huntress) master of Azmeri spirits

name: Azurite
summary: Crystal mined in Delve and spent for supplies; also the material in which Aul encased his citadel.

name: Gods as belief and Beast-energy
summary: Interpretive concept: gods in Wraeclast are sustained by worship and by proximity to the Beast's power; their abilities are 'restricted by the Beast'. Fan synthesis built from wiki statements on godhood and the Beast.

sources.locator: Lore: 'Like the other gods of Wraeclast, Kitava's abilities are restricted by the Beast'
Halani found powerless from lack of worship (see PoE1 'God' page, Maraketh gods)

name: The Beyond
summary: Plane of demons reachable via Beyond portals in Beyond league (1.2.0); Beyond demons later became a core mechanic (Beyond passives replaced Breach ones in Keepers league).

sources.locator: restrictions: Beyond passives moved to take Breach's place

name: Before Imperial Calendar (BIC)
summary: Dating convention for events preceding Imperial year 1 (e.g. Vaal fall c. 400 BIC; Vaal–Azmeri contact c. 1200 BIC).

sources.locator: The Vaal > Contacting the Azmeri; The End of Vaal Civilization (c. 400 BIC)

name: Blight (fungal growth)
summary: Fungal growths infesting Wraeclast whose mycelium spawns monster waves once a Purification Pump pierces it. Cassia first thought it a symptom of Wraeclast's death, then a parasite, and suspects a central growth that Blighted maps lead to.

name: Blightheart
summary: Hypothesised original source of the Blight. Dhunan (historical Order of the Djinn 'Blightmaster') theorised its existence; Sister Cassia independently suspects a central growth that the Blighted maps lead to. No in-game confirmation is cited.

sources.locator: member list (Dhunan) and Blight Scarabs section

name: Bloodline modifier
summary: Bloodline modifiers were shared modifiers on each pack of magic monsters in Bloodlines league; they could affect combat while the pack lived and after it died.

name: The Breach
summary: Otherworldly realm/phenomenon whose tears let Breach monsters enter Wraeclast; original Breach league (2.5.0) had breaches expanding as monsters are killed, splinters forming Breachstones for the five Breachlords' Domains. Replaced in 3.28.0 by the Keepers-of-the-Flame rework (Hiveborn, Ailith, Genesis Tree). PoE2 has Unstable Breaches and the Breachlords' lore (Xesht).

sources.locator: version history 3.28.0: new Breach replaces original Breach mechanic

name: Breach and the Keepers of the Flame (PoE2 0.5)
summary: 0.5 Breach storyline: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn from the Monastery of the Keepers; the Genesis Tree is a crafting hub; endgame Breach Domains end in Sky Fortresses with the Breachlords Tul and Esh, then Xesht.

sources.locator: Breach: Ailith and the Keepers of the Flame hold back the Hiveborn

name: Thirteen Moons
summary: Thirteen Imperial months (Verusi, Divini, Derivi, Phreci, Caspiri, Astrali, Eterni, Atziri, Vivici, Lurici, Sagari, Vitali, Azmeri), some named for renowned figures; Wraeclast has seasons.

name: Imperial Seven-Day Week
summary: Eternal seven-day week named after components of existence: Solaro, Lunaro, Fiero, Glacio, Galvano, Kaso, Sacrato.

name: Cataclysm
summary: Lore term for the world-ending catastrophes that destroyed civilisations: the unknown cataclysm that wiped out the Precursors, the Vaal Cataclysm (also 'The Fall', c. 400 BIC), and the Eternal Empire Cataclysm (~1339 IC). The corpus uses the word for each event but does not define a single in-world category; this node groups those uses. Not the PoE2 epilogue quest 'Cataclysm's Wake', which is an Atlas tutorial quest.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era to c. 1339 IC (several events)

sources.locator: intro: 'An incredibly advanced precursor civilization existed, but was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm.'; section '====The Vaal Cataclysm====': 'The Vaal Cataclysm, also known as The Fall, was a historical event...'
section '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===': 'The Cataclysm brought an end to Voll's reign and the Eternal Empire as a whole.'
page intro: 'Cataclysm's Wake is an epilogue quest. It act as the tutorial quest for the Atlas.'

name: Citadels (Iron, Copper, Stone)
summary: Three Atlas fortresses (Iron, Copper, Stone) whose bosses drop one Crisis Fragment each toward the Arbiter of Ash: Iron Citadel = Count Geonor, Copper Citadel = Jamanra, Stone Citadel = Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge (agreed by several guides; the poe2 wiki Doryani page also lists the Stone Citadel). The removed 0.1-0.4 epilogue quests Faridun Foray (boss listed Count Geonor), Ezomyte Infiltration (boss listed The Perennial King) and Vaal Incursion (boss Doryani) all start 'Investigate the Burning Monolith'; how The Perennial King maps to Jamanra is unclear. Fragment mapping differs between guides.

sources.locator: quest infobox: boss Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge; start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith'; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss Count Geonor; removed 0.5.0
quest infobox: boss The Perennial King; removed 0.5.0
can be found in endgame as a citadel boss in The Stone Citadel
Stone (Doryani), Copper (Jamanra), Iron (Count Geonor) - fragment mapping differs from other guides

name: The Cleansing Fire
summary: Cosmic force: sentient neural network of suns and black stars seeking omniscience by disintegrating what it studies; served by the Black Star and the Searing Exarch. Its all-seeing-eye symbol resembles the descry and may be origin of Templar religion (wiki inference).

sources.locator: Lycia: 'prayed to symbol of the Cleansing Fire ... Innocence appropriated it'
Cleansing Fire section: 'omnipotent neural network of suns and black stars'; symbol 'very similar to the descry'

name: Corruption
summary: Lore force of mutation and malformation tied to the Beast and its predecessors: the Beast 'possesses corrupting powers' that mutate whatever contacts it; Kitava is called 'God of Corruption' in Karui dialogue; Precursors mastered corruption and Doryani attempts to harness the Precursor Weapon to destroy corruption. Not the Corrupted-item mechanic.

chronology.relative: from the Precursor era onward (Beast, Vaal, Eternal Empire)

sources.locator: intro: 'The Beast possesses corrupting powers, devouring the souls of his prey and mutating whoever comes in contact with it.'
section '==Kitava==' > Dialogue, Haku's 'Kaom' option: 'Kitava, God of Corruption, consumed Kaom from heart to skin.'
section '===Precursor civilization===': 'After mastering corruption, they delved deeper...'; the Precursor Weapon is one 'which Doryani attempts to harness to destroy corruption'

alt_summaries.summary: The in-world corrupting power named by the Karui and Vaal (Kitava as 'God of Corruption', worship of Corruption at a Vaal temple) and carried as the Seed of Corruption (what remains of the Beast) in PoE2. The item-corruption mechanic is a separate game system.

name: Crisis Fragments
summary: Fragments needed to open the sealed door of the Burning Monolith (Arbiter of Ash). In 0.1-0.4 three were needed (Ancient, Weathered, Faded), one per Citadel boss. In the 0.5 quest log only the Ancient and Weathered fragments are picked up in the Fortress Enigma Chambers; Citadels continue to drop them for repeat runs. Guides disagree on which Citadel drops which (most: Iron=Ancient, Copper=Faded, Stone=Weathered), and the quest log matches that for Geonor (Ancient) and Doryani (Weathered).

sources.locator: Citadel-to-Arbiter loop; fragment mapping disagrees between guides

name: Darkness (Delve)
summary: Lightless darkness in the Azurite Mine that damages unprepared delvers; requires flares; Aul and Kurgal fights include a darkness phase.

name: Day Zero rule (league narrative)
summary: Dev narrative rule: each league story begins with the exile face-down on the Twilight Strand, just exiled by Dominus, so league events cannot build on what the exile did in earlier leagues. Earlier events are attributed to other exiles or remembered as memories.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule; cites 'Integrating League Stories' and ExileCon 2019 dev talks)

name: Delirium
summary: Fog of madness released through Mirrors of Delirium that spawns and strengthens monsters and can lead to the Simulacrum. Origin is only hinted: Kalandra links it to 'the Trickster' and PoE2 ties Tangmazu to a tutorial Delirium encounter.

name: Delirium: The Hare and the Raven
summary: 0.5 Delirium storyline ('The Hare and the Raven' in the press release): Elder Madox is freed from a Delirium mirror (Strange Reflection), leads the Exile to the Withered Willow, and the Raven Trickster Tangmazu must be stopped. Official notes: 'An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed, spreading madness across Wraeclast.'

sources.locator: Delirium (The Hare and the Raven): confrontation with Tangmazu
An ancient Trickster God has been unleashed

name: Doryani's contingencies
summary: Fan-synthesised reading of Doryani's secret preparations: anti-Beast Precursor weapon, flood-sealed Utzaal, and a time gateway needing Vaal blood. Interpretive; some details rest on tertiary YouTube analysis.

name: Essence
summary: Imprisoned essences freed in Essence league (2.4.0, Atlas of Worlds); modify items with guaranteed affixes; can be corrupted (Hysteria, Delirium, Horror, Insanity).

name: Exile (exile system)
summary: The exile system: criminals of Oriath are sentenced by the Templar government and shipped to Wraeclast. The sentence text reads 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. The player's character is one of these exiles. Precedent exists: under Tyndarus Phrecius, people were exiled to the land later called Trarthus. The wiki gives no single in-world reason for choosing Wraeclast.

sources.locator: section 'The Present'; section 'Reign of Tyndarus Phrecius' (Trarthus exile)

name: Exile's Journey (Day Zero rule)
summary: The wiki's 'Day Zero' rule: each league's narrative starts with the Exile face-down in the sand of the Twilight Strand, having just been exiled by Dominus, so league stories cannot build on earlier leagues' events.

sources.locator: section 'The Atlas of Worlds' (Day Zero rule)

name: Expedition and The Grand Expedition (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Expedition storyline from Ruins of Kingsmarch: Rog searches for Gwennen across an ocean of islands, Medved, Vorana, Uhtred, Olroth lead factions; a Verisium meteor is the goal.

sources.locator: Expedition: Rog searches for his missing wife, Gwennen

name: Ezomyte Runesmithing
summary: Rune craft with Kalguuran origins, revealed by Farrow in 0.5.

sources.locator: Farrow reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing

name: Forsaken Masters
summary: Seven NPC masters introduced in Forsaken Masters (1.2.0): Elreon, Haku, Vorici, Vagan, Tora, Leo and Catarina (plus Zana); they vanished at Betrayal, taken by the Syndicate (all but Zana).

name: Fragmented Memory
summary: Decaying memory sub-zones found throughout Wraeclast in Synthesis; some are memories of real events (e.g. Malachai's slave mines, gemling experiments, the Templar Laboratory) and are used by the wiki as lore sources.

sources.locator: citations of 'Abandoned Shaft Memory' and 'Eternal Residence Memory'

name: Nature of godhood (ascension)
summary: In PoE lore a mortal of rare quality could ascend to godhood on the adoration of their people, shedding mortality; this became impossible once Sin created the Beast. Becoming a god often costs one's humanity. Gods can also be 'made' by belief of followers (Innocence's ascension was fuelled by hatred of Sin).

chronology.relative: before the creation of the Beast

sources.locator: Sin, 'The Origins of the Gods': "There was a time before the Beast ... men and women like you could ascend. Through rareness of quality and the adoration of their people..."

name: Harbinger
summary: Otherworldly enemies of Harbinger league (3.0.0) beaten by killing their minions; drop currency shards.

name: Heart of the Grove
summary: Plant that grows from a harvested Tier 4 Sacred Grove seed (about 100 growth cycles). Harvesting it is the challenge that leads to the Avatar of the Grove; Oshabi herself turns into it after the tutorial quest.

sources.locator: League mechanic: Heart of the Grove
Lead: Oshabi turns into the Heart of the Grove

name: Eternal calendar
summary: Calendar of 1 IC (Imperialis Conceptus), seven days and thirteen moons (Verusi, Divini, Derivi ... Azmeri).

name: Eternal slave trade
summary: Under Chitus the Empire enslaved Karui, Ezomytes and Maraketh, sending them to mines and cities.

name: Intrinsic darkness
summary: Tane's term for the cruelty/ill-will in living beings that Metamorphs distil from monster organs; he now thinks it older and more universal than Corruption and hopes to destroy it while leaving the flesh unharmed.

name: Kalguuran runesmithing
summary: Kalguuran art of engraving starlight runes (Verisium from meteorites) into weapons and armour; Ezomytes learned it from the first expedition; revived as Runesmithing in Settlers and Runeforging in PoE2 Act 4.

name: Karui Gods
summary: The gods honoured within the Karui Way: Arohongui, Hinekora, Kitava, Ngamahu, Ramako, Tasalio, Tawhoa, Tukohama and Valako, as named on the Karui Gods page.

sources.locator: intro: 'In the game's lore, The Karui Way has several gods that are representative of or rule over various aspects of the world.'

name: Karui Way (Makanui)
summary: Karui code of honour and traditions (Way of the Warrior); some who follow it forbid virtue gems for causing blood fever.

name: The Kingsmarch Charter
summary: Royal charter under which Kingsmarch operates; Johan enforces it to the letter, including punishments such as the Royal Order of Criminal Hanging subject to a statute of limitations.

name: Kingsmarch shipping and trade routes
summary: Trade shipping from Kingsmarch to Kalguuran ports (Riben Fell, Pondium, Kalguur) and Karui ports (Ngakanu, Te Onui, Moti Aro); risks include pirates, corrupt officials, a royal tax and 'mysterious green light' losses. Pirate Admiral Valerius can commandeer ships.

name: Kingsmarch workers and town management
summary: Recruited workers (miners, smelters, farmers, disenchanters, shippers, Atlas runners) are hired through Raulf for Gold; the town runs on real-time resources: ores, bars, crops and thaumaturgic dust.

name: Leylines
summary: Ancient underground structures Doryani believes span the continent beneath the Ziggurat; they power the Waygate and resonate with the Precursor Tower.

sources.locator: Doryani: This Ziggurat was built over what my ancestors called 'leylines'

name: Lifeforce
summary: Oshabi's name for the invisible force that revives the dead and shapes beasts and plants, released by Grove seeds in Wild, Vivid and Primal forms; she notes its similarity to Corruption and calls them perhaps 'two sides of the same leaf'.

sources.locator: Dialogue: Lifeforce, The Slaying of Malachai, Monsters

name: Lord's Trial
summary: Azmerian maze-festival to choose chieftains; raised Veruso to power and inspired Izaro's Labyrinth.

name: Maraketh Shrine
summary: Room-reward shrines in the PoE2 Trial of the Sekhemas. Each shrine (Tabina, Balbala, Ahkeli or Galai variants) lets the player spend 5 Sacred Water to restore part of their Honour, with a random Boon or Minor Affliction on some variants; the Fountain of Youth minor boon restores 40 Honour when a Maraketh Shrine is venerated.

sources.locator: Full page (stub): 'Maraketh Shrines are found as room rewards in the Trial of the Sekhemas'; shrine list (Honour Tabina / Balbala / Ahkeli / Galai); Fountain of Youth minor boon

name: Martyr of the First Edict (Void league leaderboard)
summary: Rise of the Abyssal mechanic: once per league a level-100 character can be sacrificed at the Site of the Chosen, sending it to the Void league and listing it as the 'Martyr of the First Edict' on the leaderboard. Meta/league flavour; no source explains the naming.

sources.locator: paragraph: 'listed as the Martyr of the First Edict on the leaderboard'

name: Masters of the Atlas
summary: 0.5 storylines of three Atlas Masters: Jado (Order of the Djinn; unlocked by an anomaly map near the start), Hilda (monster hunter, Hilda's Campsite) and Doryani (unlocked by clearing a corruption nexus). The earlier draft's 'ascendancy-like specialisation' claim is unsupported and was removed.

sources.locator: Atlas Masters: Jado, Hilda, Doryani; Doryani questline via corruption nexus; Jado via anomaly map

name: Memory Tears and Threads
summary: Tears in Atlas reality where Zana's manifested memories leak; Eagon traces threads to Moments of Loneliness, Trauma, Reverence.

name: Nemesis modifier
summary: Nemesis modifiers were powerful extra modifiers on every rare monster in Nemesis league (hardcore); the league modifier was "Rare Monsters each have a Nemesis Mod".

name: The Pantheon
summary: Pantheon power system introduced by Sin after Tukohama's death: Sin captures the souls of the risen gods the exile kills in Part Two and lends the exile a small portion of their power. The Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris and Lunaris grant major god powers; Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha, Ralakesh, Gruthkul, Yugul, Garukhan and Shakari are minor gods.

sources.locator: After Tukohama: Sin introduces the Pantheon
'Sin is able to capture the souls of the Pantheon of gods'
Garukhan is a minor pantheon goddess

name: Atlas of Worlds (PoE2)
summary: The PoE2 endgame map network, reached after the campaign via Doryani's Waygate and navigated with Waystones. Rebuilt in 0.5 (Return of the Ancients) with fixed points of interest, storylines and a fully unlockable Atlas passive tree.

sources.locator: quest log: 'Use the Map Device and the Waystone to enter a Map'
Atlas passive tree: Fully remade; zone quest chains

name: Prophecy
summary: Prophecy system of Prophecy league (2.3.0); removed in 3.17.0; Pale Council bosses.

name: The Red Pyre
summary: Entity/title in Ailith's Word of the Dreamer ('The Red Pyre burns hot... The Dreamer once knew him, before his addiction'). The fire imagery and the book's subject (the four Breachlords that became Xesht) point to Xoph, Dark Embers; the identification is inferred, not stated.

name: Rite of the Nameless
summary: Ritual mechanic/quest stage: place the Head of the King on the Incomplete Effigy in Caer Tarth, use it to select five maps, complete Rituals there to collect effigy parts (Tangled Torso, Mossy Arm, Frayed Cloth, Brittle Arm, Ragged Cloth), activate the Effigy and perform the Rite to reach the Darkness and the Bodach. 0.5.5 campaign unique-boss Rituals work similarly.

sources.locator: unique boss Rituals work similarly to the Rite of the Nameless

name: Ritual (altar mechanic)
summary: Ritual Altars spawn wave encounters inside a ritual circle; defeating monsters earns Favour/Tribute to buy items. PoE1 Ritual league gives no narrative; Vaal Ritual Altars may summon Atziri's Apparition; later Wildwood lore ties 'ritual altars' to the King in the Mists; PoE2 adopts it in Forbidden Rites.

name: Ritual and the King in the Mists (PoE2)
summary: 0.5 Ritual storyline: Aoife, a lost spirit bound by the King in the Mists, appeals to the Wildwood; the prison beneath holds the Bodach; the Rite of the Nameless in Caer Tarth. 0.5.5 adds Ritual altars to every zone.

sources.locator: Ritual: Aoife, a lost spirit, bound by the King in the Mists... Bodach ... Rite of the Nameless

name: Rogue exiles
summary: Exiled criminals who roam Wraeclast as hostile NPCs; originated in Anarchy league (0.11.0), later reused in PoE2 (Lichborn exiles in Rise of the Abyssal).

sources.locator: raising a rogue exile as Lichborn

name: Rogue Exiles (PoE2)
summary: Roaming exile NPC bosses introduced in 0.2.0; Abyss can raise a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile.

sources.locator: raising a slain rogue exile as a Lichborn exile

name: Royal Order of Criminal Hanging
summary: A royal order to hang named criminals that was damaged by seawater on the voyage to Kingsmarch; Johan declined to enforce it because the reply would exceed the Charter's statute of limitations and he would not hang the wrong man.

sources.locator: ==Legal Response (Johan)==: "the recent Royal Order of Criminal Hanging was damaged by seawater"; "the punishment in question will exceed the Charter statute of limitations"

name: Sekhema
summary: Maraketh leader title; always a woman chosen by merit and anointed with the feather of the Great Roc; tale-women keep the people's history.

name: Shrine (Domination)
summary: Shrines are a mechanic introduced by Domination league (1.0.0); Domination's area modifier allowed shrines to spawn.

sources.locator: lead: 'This league introduced shrines'; Modifier section

name: Strongbox
summary: Strongboxes are a mechanic introduced by Ambush league (1.1.0, March 2014); every area in Ambush carried the Ambush chests modifier.

name: Tempest
summary: Tempests are effects introduced by Tempest league that can change monster and player size, cause damage, alter drop rates, or animate weapons that drop; affected areas are shown on the World Screen.

name: Thaumaturgy
summary: Gem-based magic whose source is the Beast. Outlawed by Veruso, embraced by Chitus under Malachai's 'Thaumatocracy', and banned again by Voll.

name: The Decay
summary: Ancient cosmic mould-like entity ('the Oblivion') from outside time and space that turns all it touches to void; the Elder is its servant. Dormant after the Elder's defeat.

name: The Edicts (Precursor murals)
summary: Series of vague Precursor murals described by the PoE2 wiki as depicting the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it; numbered First to Fourth in game. Known: Third = instrument is the Weapon (Hooded One recognises it as 'the Weapon I saw in that third mural'); Second = Doryani's guess that the Seed was its instrument; Fourth = investigated in the Epilogue after the Arbiter of Ash (PoE1 wiki editors speculate it caused the Great Fire); First = unexplained threat averted in the Epilogue. The full text of the edicts is not given in any source read. Not to be confused with Count Geonor's hanging edicts in Ogham.

chronology.relative: Precursor age, far older than the Vaal and Winter of the World

sources.locator: 'It was depicted in their Edicts, vague murals that depicts the Beast and possibly instructions on how to contain it.'
Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'
Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural'; Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'

name: The Pantheon (soul-capture mechanic)
summary: Game mechanic and lore device by which Sin captures the essences of slain gods and grants the Exile a fraction of their powers. Major gods: Brine King, Arakaali, Solaris, Lunaris. Minor gods: Tukohama, Abberath, Ryslatha (Act 6), Gruthkul, Ralakesh (Act 7), Yugul (Act 8), Garukhan, Shakari (Act 9).

sources.locator: section 'The Pantheon'; Sin dialogue 'The Father of War': "While a god may fall, their essence lingers... That essence can be yours"

name: The Struggle
summary: Ancient conflict among cosmic forces (the Decay, the Tangle, the Cleansing Fire) introduced by the Envoy. The forces cannot clash directly without rending reality, so disputes are settled by duels between mortal champions. The Elder's defeat left a vacancy over the Atlas that drew the others in; the Maven, with the Exile as her champion and Kirac's Vanguard, stands against the Eldritch champions. A progenitor/Lightkeeper is cited as the order the forces are blind to.

sources.locator: lead: 'defeat of the Elder ... created a temporary vacancy'

name: The Tangle
summary: Cosmic force served by the Infinite Hunger and the Eater of Worlds (flavour: sea of limbs, to eat, to feast).

name: Timeless Conflict
summary: Legions of different factions (Karui, Maraketh, Templar, Eternal Empire, Vaal) frozen in stasis by a timeless monolith, locked in an endless battle; broken out of stasis by damaging them. Why they are frozen is not explained in the wiki.

name: Tormented spirits
summary: Spirits of tormented criminals in Torment league (1.3.0) that flee, empower nearby monsters and drop loot; unrelated to Kitava's Torments in Act 5.

name: Trial of Chaos
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 3 at the Temple of Chaos via an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the quest item Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian). Based on the PoE1 Ultimatum league and overseen by the Trialmaster.

sources.locator: intro: 'The Trialmaster ... oversee the Trials of Chaos'

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial in the Temple of Chaos (first in Act 3), a gauntlet run with an Inscribed Ultimatum; the Trialmaster offers modifiers and rewards. Mechanically based on PoE1's Ultimatum.

name: Trial of the Sekhemas
summary: A PoE2 Ascension Trial first accessible in Act 2 via the Djinn Barya key (or the quest item Balbala's Barya), a gauntlet of up to 4 floors with bosses including Rattlecage, Hadi and Rafiq, Ashar and Zarokh.

alt_summaries.summary: Ascension trial first accessible in Act 2 via a Djinn Barya on the Relic Altar; a gauntlet governed by Honour, Boons and Afflictions; based on PoE1's Forbidden Sanctum.

name: Uber pinnacle bosses
summary: Harder repeatable versions: Uber Elder, Uber Sirus, Uber Maven, Uber Exarch/Eater after 24 influenced T14+ maps. Memory-version retellings per Day Zero.

name: Utopia (Twilight Order ideal)
summary: The Order's promised god-free world ('without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity'), recruited for with 'Accept Utopia! Embrace the saviour!'. Art book: intention is good but its methods are contentious.

name: Vaal corruption and thaumaturgical technology
summary: Vaal science combined gem-craft, constructs, mechanical technology and corruption drawn from the Beast; much of it was developed by Doryani and housed at Atzoatl and Utzaal. Its influence resurfaces as Vaal side areas, Vaal skill gems and Vaal Orbs in PoE1.

name: Vaal sacrifice and Vaal souls
summary: Vaal bloodpriests discovered that the souls of the recently killed briefly seek another source of life and can be captured in a vaal skill gem to empower it; human and blood sacrifice powered Vaal constructs and society, and slavery supplied victims.

name: Verisium
summary: Metal ore found only in fallen meteorites and not native to Wraeclast; Kalguuran runes were typically crafted from it, and in PoE2 Act 4 Dannig forges Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots.

sources.locator: ===Runes===: "Runes were typically crafted using Verisium, a type of metal ore found only from fallen meteorites, and not native to Wraeclast."
Bring the Verisium to Dannig / Take the Verisium Spikes from Dannig: Dannig crafts Verisium Spikes from Verisium Ingots
Remnants can contain Verisium used in Runeforging
Seek out the crater of a fallen star, a meteor of pure Verisium

alt_summaries.summary: Ore from remnants and a meteor; enables Runeforging and Runic Ward.

name: Virtue Gems
summary: Gems from the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy, buried by Veruso and mined by slaves under Chitus; infused into gemlings. Ubiquitous in Vaal society.

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri term for virtue gems, which they are forbidden to touch; contact causes a horrific reaction.
Gems discovered under Mount Veruso that the Vaal used to gain great power; Vaal bodies were adorned and later socketed with gems, and the Vaal never shared the secret with the Azmeri.

name: Wildwood ascendancy classes
summary: Affliction's temporary ascendancies (Wildwood Primalist with charms, Warden of the Maji with tinctures, Warlock of the Mists with corpse items) earned through the Azmeri questlines; removed at league end.

name: Humours / Wisps (Wildwood)
summary: In the Viridian Wildwood the four humours (Primal, Vivid, Wild, Sacred) materialise as wisps. The first three share names with Harvest's Primal, Vivid and Wild Lifeforce colours. Sacred humours are harvested by the ritual altars of the King in the Mists.

name: Hiveborn
summary: Breach-spawn into which the Breachlords were evolving; the Keepers of the Flame, founded through Chayula's dreams, exist to destroy them. The Dreamer is revealed to be of the same kind as the Hiveborn.

sources.locator: Lore: the Breachlords began their evolution into the Hiveborn; the Dreamer is the same creature as the Hiveborn

alt_summaries.summary: Mutated Breach monsters spilling into Wraeclast through a stabilised interdimensional link.
Breach monsters invading Wraeclast in the reworked Breach; fought by the Exile and Ailith, source of Graftblood and Hiveblood.

name: Kitava's Heart
summary: A part of Kitava that spawns during its battle in Act 5 (Cathedral Rooftop, The Feeding Trough) and Act 10. Introduced as a boss monster in 3.0.0; since 3.2.0 it cannot be slowed below its base speed.

sources.locator: lead: 'Kitava's Heart is a part of Kitava that spawns during the battle with Kitava, the Insatiable, which occurs in Act 5 and Act 10'; Version history 3.0.0 'Introduced to the game as boss monster'; 3.2.0 speed note

name: The Lightless (Abyssals)
summary: Ancient subterranean race created, not born, via necromancy, afraid of light; invaded during the Winter of the World and were driven back underground by the returning sun. Antagonists of Abyss and PoE2 Rise of the Abyssals.

sources.locator: The Winter of the World > The Lightless

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient necromantic race, the Abyssals ('the spawn of the Well of Souls' per the Hooded One), serving Kulemak through Lich Lords; they emerge through Abyss fissures. Ancient alliances fought them for centuries in the Winter of the World.

name: Metamorph
summary: Shape-shifting enemies assembled from organs of other monsters and bosses; they use the moves of whatever parts they carry.

name: Scourge monsters
summary: Blood-crazed demonic monsters of the Scourge Nightmare realm. After the league they became the core game's Beyond monsters, and currencies such as Tainted Blessing came from them.

name: Synthetes
summary: Synthesis league bosses (Altered, Augmented, Rewritten and Twisted Synthete) guarding fractured uniques; later unique-map bosses.

sources.locator: unique items paragraph listing Altered/Augmented/Rewritten/Twisted Synthete

name: The Nameless
summary: Shadowy beings born with the Wildwood as the 'unseen reflection opposite the mortal world'; led by the King in the Mists; Gruthkul was one.

name: The Titans
summary: Primordial race that walked molten Wraeclast and inhabited its volcanoes; mostly indifferent to humans; nearly wiped out in the 'rising darkness', with the Molten One the sole survivor.

name: Trarthan mercenaries
summary: Lawless Trarthan veterans met in Mercenaries league; hirable allies with unique gear and skills; noble ones come from the four Great Houses.

name: The Undying
summary: Gemlings and citizens of Sarn transformed by the Cataclysm into mindless monsters that can live for centuries; some gemling legionnaires later regain sentience (Act 8 Grain Gate).

name: Vorniculia / horrors
summary: Horror species that attacked Kalguuran outposts; Olroth's Knights culled the Vorniculia.

name: Wisps (humours)
summary: Wildwood humours materialised as Primal, Vivid, Wild and Sacred wisps; freed wisps escape into the overworld empowering monsters; Sacred humours are harvested by the King in the Mists' ritual altars.

name: Abberath, the Cloven One
summary: Goatman god (the Cloven One, Quaffer of Souls) killed in the Valley of the Fire Drinker. Per Bestel, goatmen offer him humans and he eats them 'meat, soul and all'; per Sin he was once Abberath the Scholar King, an alchemist who burned flesh away to drink the life force within, starting with goats. Minor Pantheon god.

sources.locator: Bestel: 'when the goatmen find him a ... human... he eats them'
Act 6 dialogue "Abberath": the Scholar King, Quaffer of Souls

alt_summaries.summary: Former scholar who consumed souls of goats and became the goat-like Cloven One; father of the Faun; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

name: Arakaali, Spinner of Shadows
summary: Vaal spider-goddess of love and death, worshipped by Azmeri artists; consorts with Silk in the Temple of Decay and is killed as Act 7's boss. A relationship with Sin is hinted.

sources.locator: 'lesser relationships with ... Arakaali' (cites PoE2 Arakaali's Lust)

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal harlot turned fertility goddess and queen, the Spinner of Shadows; held Sin captive; sealed in the Temple of Decay and slain by the Exile in Act 7.
Spinner of Shadows: mortal temptress turned arachnid, Vaal goddess of fertility, first worshipped by the Azmeri; her temple is the Temple of Decay (Act 7).

name: Arohongui, Daughter of the Moon
summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. Daughter of Ramako's alleged impersonator and Sione; lacks the warmth and light of the Sun

alt_summaries.summary: Karui moon goddess, Daughter of the Moon; daughter of Ramako and Lani Lua in myth (possibly Tangmazu's child).

name: The Beast
summary: Divine creature, source of thaumaturgy and corruption, grown by Sin from the Dark Ember beneath Highgate to keep the gods asleep. Has no will of its own; exploited by Doryani, Atziri, Chitus, Malachai. The Exile kills it in Act 4; PoE2 follows a new Beast grown from the stolen Seed of Corruption.

alt_summaries.summary: Gigantic Dark Ember creature sealed under Highgate, killed by the Exile in Act 4; its death weakens the gods' restraint.
Gods-lulling Dark Ember creature killed in Act 4.

Creature grown by Sin from the Dark Ember to lull the gods into sleep and prevent mortal ascension to godhood; killed by the exile in Act 4, which freed the gods and the souls of Malachai's lieutenants.
Ancient divine creature grown from the Seed of Corruption by Sin; in PoE2 a Beast carried across the Vastiri on the Faridun Dreadnought and fed corpses by the Countess's plan.
Ancient divine creature of thaumaturgy, created by Sin from the Seed of Corruption; Atziri and Doryani manipulated it.

name: The Brine King
summary: Azmeri king Tsoagoth turned god of storms and sea, worshipped by the Brinerot pirates with sacrifices; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

sources.locator: Nessa: 'his majesty could never be satiated on his wedding day by one bride alone'

alt_summaries.summary: Sea god who turns Nessa into a mermaid to wed her; Act 6 final boss in his reef, whose domain was the city of Tsoatha.

name: Chaos
summary: Impulse able to see across timelines, once worshipped by Vaal priests; master of the Trialmaster and enemy-of-sorts to Hinekora's fixed prophecies.

sources.locator: intro and section 'Interactions with other characters'
Community Team post: 'Chaos does not know what you truly are...'

alt_summaries.summary: An Impulse, a beyond-godlike being and the flip of the coin, who can see multiple timelines and is the master of the Trialmaster. Worshipped by the Vaal. The Blood Crucible was a pact between Chaos and the Vaal High Priests.

Impulse, a godlike entity that sees all possibilities across timelines and delights in mortals bending chance; once worshipped by the Vaal; master of the Trialmaster; opposed to Order. Aware that the exiles exist in parallel timelines (dev statement).

Impulse of Chaos, not a Vaal god, but a sect of Vaal priests worshipped him; his Temple of Chaos stood on the outskirts of Utzaal. The Trialmaster says Atziri's realm lies beyond his reach and the Vaal fall occurred in every timeline.

name: Chayula, the Dreamer
summary: Breachlord known as the Dreamer or Benevolent Dreamer; PoE2 lore shows he aided the Third Pact alliance, was severed from the failed Breachlord merge, and formed the Keepers of the Flame through dreams. After Xesht falls Ailith reveals his ultimate aim is to subjugate all life as obedient thralls.

sources.locator: Lore: the Dreamer is Chayula, a Breachlord
Lore: after Xesht is defeated Ailith tells the player the Dreamer's true intent

alt_summaries.summary: One of five Breachlords (chaos). Boss of Chayula's Domain (male per wiki). As the Dreamer (Keepers league) he opposes the Xesht fusion. Original Breach bosses introduced in 2.5.0 (Chayula to the core game 2.6.0 per wiki version history), removed 3.28.0.
Breachlord worshipped at Atzoatl by the Cult of Purple Flame.

name: Craiceann, First of the Deep
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Deep ('First of All'), ancestor of crabs, squid and sea creatures; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the deep.

name: The Eater of Worlds
summary: Eldritch Horror serving the Tangle, fought in Absence of Symmetry and Harmony.

name: Esh, Forked Thought
summary: One of five Breachlords. Lightning damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Esh's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

sources.locator: boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other

alt_summaries.summary: Breachlord (Esh) fought as a paired boss with its counterpart in the Hive Colony (PoE2 0.5); they share a health bar in the final phase and drop the Breachlord Sac.

name: Farrul, First of the Plains
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Plains ('First of the Hunt'), ancestor of hounds, cats and other mammals; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the plains.

name: Fenumus, First of the Night
summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Night ('First Explorer'), ancestor of bugs and insectoids; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the night; wove a net during the Great Fire.

name: Garukhan
summary: Goddess of wind and sky, formerly the Maraketh Sekhema Orbala ('Sekhema of Sekhemas'); freed Sin from the cliff where Innocence's followers had chained him, became his lover and wife and bore Shakari; Sin planted the Dark Ember 'for Garukhan'.

sources.locator: 'Garukhan, Queen of the Wind' (Orbala; Chains of Castigation, Blood of Innocence, Sin 'Garukhan' dialogue)
Relationships: Sin was wed to Garukhan

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh storm goddess, Queen of the Winds; wife of Sin, mother of Shakari; formerly the hero Orbala, Sekhema of Sekhemas (PoE2). Slain by the Exile in Act 9 at Sin's request.

Maraketh goddess ('Vulture of the Wastes', Queen of the Winds), wife of Sin and mother of Shakari; in PoE2 she is revealed to have been the mortal Sekhema Orbala. Killed in the Quarry in Act 9 after Kira's attempted sacrifice of Oyun. Minor Pantheon god.

The PoE1 wiki's Orbala page says PoE2 identifies Garukhan as the ascended Orbala (mortal Maraketh warrior); the PoE1 wiki and PoE2 quests do not fully confirm this, so it stays inferred. The Horn of the Vastiri quest retraces Orbala's footsteps.

name: The God of Domination
summary: Mysterious, possibly otherworldly god tied to the Harbingers; Harbinger uniques foretell its gaze falling over Wraeclast.

name: The Goddess of Justice
summary: Deity worshipped by Izaro Phrecius; known only by this title.

name: The Greatwolf
summary: First Ones-type god of the hunt and ancestor of wolves and werewolves; possessed Rigwald, the Wolven King, during the Purity Rebellion.

alt_summaries.summary: Ezomyte First One that possessed Thane Rigwald after he sought its power in the Purity Rebellion.

name: Gruthkul
summary: Bestial minor god, Mother of Despair / Porcelain Queen, a mother whose children were slaughtered by Arakaali and whose grief made her a horned beast; Act 7 Pantheon boss. Sources disagree on the culprit: the God page says Arakaali slaughtered her children; Sin's dialogue says the Vaal laid waste to her kingdom; Sin's 'Mother of Despair' dialogue says her daughters plotted against Arakaali.

sources.locator: Sin: 'The Vaal laid waste to her kingdom and placed her slaughtered children at her feet.'
Act 7 dialogue "The Mother of Despair": the daughters plotted against Arakaali

alt_summaries.summary: Grieving mother-goddess whose kingdom the Vaal laid waste and whose children were slaughtered; mad with the wish to share her grief, she is killed in the Den of Despair (Dread Thicket). Sin hints that her daughters had plotted against Arakaali, who left her web only when forced to. Minor Pantheon god.

name: Halani
summary: Forgotten Maraketh water goddess, found powerless and dying from lack of worship in PoE2 Act 2 Buried Shrines; mother of Azarian.

sources.locator: Walkthrough 'Talk to the Water Goddess' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'

alt_summaries.summary: Water goddess lying in a shrine at the heart of Keth. She asks the Exile to burn her with Everburning Cinders to end her suffering.

name: Hinekora
summary: Karui goddess, the Mother of Death, ruler of the Halls of the Dead, seer of prophecy; speaks through the Well of Passing and rewards the worthy with the Tattoo of Hinekora.

sources.locator: Peer into the Well of Passing

alt_summaries.summary: Karui Mother of Death; collects souls in the Halls of the Dead, foresees events across timelines, whipped Kitava into the underworld with her hair, and slept after foreseeing the Slumbering of the Gods. Oversees the Trial of the Ancestors.
Karui goddess of death; could not see Doryani in the past.

name: Innocence
summary: Templar god of light and purity, twin of Sin; per Lycia's relics his ascension was fuelled by turning followers against Sin. In Act 5 High Templar Avarius is his vessel; after Sin's 'more sensible host' (Bannon) sacrifices himself with the Staff of Purity in Act 10, he is reborn, helps defeat Kitava and then goes into self-exile in the far south.

sources.locator: section 'Lore' (Innocence defeated in Act 5; re-awakened by Bannon for Act 10)
Avarius as vessel of Innocence (see Kitava page: Triumph of Innocence)
quest An End to Hunger/Death and Rebirth: Bannon resurrects Innocence
Lore: stained glass windows, Original Sin
Bannon: 'it has the ability to revitalize Innocence into waking fully'
Innocence: "Bone and corruption shall not impede the path of purity!"

alt_summaries.summary: The god the Templars worship as saviour. Sin captures Innocence's soul; Avarius becomes its vessel and Innocence is defeated in Act 5. Re-awakened by Bannon's sacrifice, it helps defeat Kitava in Act 10.
Templar god, twin of Sin; ascended using hatred of Sin; Oriath's founding deity; also Maxarius.
Templar god of purity, twin brother of Sin; his vessel Avarius is killed by the Exile; his fall allows Kitava's summoning.
Sin's twin brother and a Templar god; hosted by High Templar Avarius, destroyed in Act 5 and in Act 10 resurrected when Bannon sacrifices himself, then destroys Kitava's Horns to help the exile.

name: Kamasa
summary: Vaal god of Wealth, represented by a monkey; in PoE2 Act 3 monkey-statue temples in Utzaal hold Kamasa treasure.

sources.locator: Orb of Sacrifice named for Kamasa

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal Monkey God of wealth and greed; mentioned in PoE2 Act 2/3 and in PoE1 items.

name: Kitava
